newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian unionist blasts sacking of TV head.
newsitem.headline: Romanian unionist blasts sacking of TV head.

text.p: A top trade unionist on Tuesday denounced the government's dismissal of Romanian state television's general manager, saying it was a blatant attempt to take control of broadcasting.

"This is a political step and we are against political interference of any kind," Dumitru Iuga, leader of the television employees trade union said by telephyone. "They are only trying to have a television of their own."
The ex-communist opposition, ousted in last month's election, joined Iuga in saying Dumitru Popa's dismissal was illegal. They said only parliament had the right to sack him.
State television, subservient to parliament by law, still broadcasts largely dull fare seven years after the fall of communism and is far behind private rivals in major cities.
But it is the only channel able to reach all corners of the country of 23 million.

Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea announced Popa's dismissal on Monday. He was replaced as interim head by Stere Gulea, a prominent member of a political party which two years ago broke with the Democratic Convention (CDR), the main bloc within the new governing coalition
Ciorbea said the appointment corrected a legal anomaly left by the outgoing government, under which Popa was both head of television and a member of national radio's executive board.

When in opposition, the CDR repeatedly accused state television of serving the interests of the ruling leftists. Iuga staged a four-week hunger strike in 1995 to denounce what he said were political appointments within the broadcast media.
